title: CPF Members with MediSave Contributions in Arrears and Proposed Waivers to Allow Them to Access Government Grants
what_it_is: CPF Members with MediSave Contributions in Arrears and Proposed Waivers to Allow Them to Access Government Grants

sections.label: SEP MediSave obligations and Workfare
sections.summary: Most SEPs meet MediSave obligations; those who cannot may get extended GIRO or case-by-case appeal flexibilities to qualify for Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: More than 75% of SEPs are able to meet their MediSave obligations in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the remaining SEPs who are unable to do so, about 50% of them have less than $3,000 in outstanding liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Most SEPs with outstanding MediSave liabilities have not met the Basic Healthcare Sum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To ensure that SEPs continue to take personal responsibility in saving for their longer-term retirement and healthcare needs, SEPs are required to contribute to their MediSave to qualify for Government schemes, such as Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To enable our lower-income SEPs to benefit from Workfare, SEPs have up to two years to make the required MediSave contributions to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Less than 5% of appeals for Workfare were from SEPs requesting to waive their MediSave contribution requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board has been helping SEPs who are facing difficulties in meeting their MediSave obligations find alternative arrangements, such as by extending their GIRO arrangements to reduce monthly instalments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Board also considers appeals on a case-by-case basis and exercises flexibilities based on the appellants' needs.
